clue.text: Hunter with dreadful curse has to be kept inside

indicators.note: has is held within the scrambled letters of curse
dreadful suggests something wrecked, so the letters of curse are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A huntsman swears horribly and has to be locked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hunter' looks like a description of a person in the surface story, but it is the definition, from the French for huntsman.
explanation.definitionFit: A chasseur is French for a huntsman, and the word also names a light-infantry soldier.

clue.text: Tough little pieces skinned

indicators.note: with its skin removed, the word for little pieces loses its outer letters at both ends

parts.note: shards are small broken fragments

explanation.surface: Small fragments that have had their peel taken off are tough to chew.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard and tough are synonyms for something resistant or difficult.

clue.text: Keeling over, said to be legless in pub or restaurant

indicators.note: the trimmed letters sit inside the word for pub

parts.note: an inn is a pub

indicators.note: legless means losing the bottom, so the reversed word drops its last letter
keeling over is toppling, so the word said is turned backwards

explanation.surface: Someone collapses, reportedly blind drunk, at the pub or a curry house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keeling over' turns SAID into DIAS; 'legless' cuts its last letter to DIA, which goes 'in' INN. 'Legless' looks like British slang for drunk, and 'said' like a homophone signal.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain an Indian is everyday shorthand for a curry house, a restaurant serving South Asian food.

clue.text: Very slow girl eats up single calorie

indicators.note: the girl takes the following letters inside her

parts.note: gal is an informal word for a girl

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters read from bottom to top, reversed

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one, a single

explanation.surface: A sluggish girl consumes one calorie at a time.
explanation.walkthrough: I + CAL read 'up' gives LACI, which GAL 'eats': G + LACI + AL.
explanation.definitionFit: Glacial describes the pace of a glacier, so idiomatically it means extremely slow.

clue.text: How to go from capitals of Spain, Russia, Qatar and Peru.

wordplay.reading: S, R, Q, P: a journey from the first letter to the last

parts.words: How to go from capitals of Spain, Russia, Qatar and Peru
parts.note: capitals here are first letters, so the four countries give a run of four letters, and the route is from the first of them to the last

explanation.surface: A puzzle about travelling between four countries' capital cities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capitals' looks like Madrid, Moscow, Doha and Lima, but it means initial letters: S, R, Q, P, which go from S TO P. The definition is the full stop after Peru.
explanation.definitionFit: In British English the punctuation mark is called a full stop, so the dot itself is a definition.

clue.text: Ideas at home on cooking venison with a bit of thyme

parts.note: to be in is to be at home

indicators.note: cooking turns ingredients into something new, so these letters are rearranged
only the first letter of thyme is used

explanation.surface: Fresh ideas from someone at home preparing venison with a sprig of herb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a bit of thyme' supplies only its first letter, which joins the venison before the cooking.
explanation.definitionFit: Inventions are things devised in the mind, so in the sense of creations or notions they are ideas.

clue.text: Master race's talisman

parts.note: Ascot is a famous English horse race meeting

explanation.surface: An item of luck belonging to a sinister 'master race'.
explanation.walkthrough: Ascot is a famous racecourse and race meeting in England; the 's is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A mascot is an object or figure kept to bring good luck, just like a charm.

clue.text: Loose coins ruin her plans

indicators.note: to ruin plans is to wreck them, so the letters of her plans are scrambled

explanation.surface: Some loose change upsets a woman's plans.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrapnel is British slang for a pocketful of small change, by analogy with metal fragments.

clue.text: 3 vehicle clamped in Kensington Gardens

indicators.note: the answer is held fast within the letters of the London park's name

explanation.surface: A car wheel-clamped in a London park.
explanation.walkthrough: 3 points to the answer at 3 down, Indian; Kensington Gardens is a royal park in London.
explanation.definitionFit: A tonga is a light two-wheeled horse-drawn carriage used in India, so it is an Indian vehicle.

clue.text: Perhaps Washington Post journalist took drugs

parts.note: the Washington Post is an example of something American, US
ED, short for editor, is the crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter at a major US newspaper has been taking narcotics.
explanation.definitionFit: To use is slang for taking illegal substances, so used means having taken them.

clue.text: Current head of school quits physics, say, about little cash at the beginning

parts.note: in means current or fashionable

indicators.note: the trimmed word goes around the small sum
quits means the head of school leaves the word

parts.note: physics is an example of a science

indicators.note: only the first letter of school is used

parts.note: I P reads as one penny, a small amount of money

explanation.surface: A school head abandons physics for small money matters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little cash' is one penny written as I P, a numeral one beside the penny abbreviation; 'Current' is the fashionable sense, not electricity.
explanation.definitionFit: Incipience is the state of starting or coming into being, so it names an onset.

clue.text: Trotsky buys pint with old money

indicators.note: to buy is to take in, so the name holds the abbreviation

parts.note: Leon Trotsky, the Russian revolutionary

explanation.surface: A revolutionary pays for a beer with obsolete currency.
explanation.definitionFit: The lepton was a small coin of Greece, a hundredth of a drachma, before the euro.

clue.text: Dire Straits event has no new time for parodies

indicators.note: dire means terrible, so the letters of straits event are rearranged
the letters for new and time are taken out of the fodder

explanation.surface: A Dire Straits concert loses its novelty and becomes a send-up.
explanation.walkthrough: Dire Straits were a British rock band, but 'Dire' is the anagram signal; take N and T out of STRAITS EVENT and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Travesties are absurd or grotesque imitations, much like mocking spoofs.

clue.text: Taste a delicate starter of pâté beforehand

indicators.note: the letter comes before the word for delicate
only the opening letter of pâté is used

parts.note: petite means small and dainty, delicate

explanation.surface: Sample a dainty appetizer of pâté before the meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A taste for something is a liking or desire, the same as an appetite for it.

clue.text: Even Dad's starting to recede

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father

indicators.note: only the first letter of recede is used

explanation.surface: Even Father's hairline is beginning to go back.
explanation.definitionFit: On a par means equal, so par expresses being level or even.

clue.text: Scoundrel breaks into song in rural paradise

indicators.note: the rogue forces his way inside the word for song

parts.note: an aria is an operatic solo song
a cad is a dishonourable man

explanation.surface: A rogue bursts into song in an idyllic countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: Arcadia is the pastoral Greek region idealized in poetry as an unspoilt rustic utopia.

clue.text: Perhaps 3 in 1,000?

definitions.note: 3 down is Indian, and Indian is an example of a type of ink

parts.note: K stands for a thousand (kilo)

explanation.surface: A riddle asking whether three might be found within a thousand.
explanation.walkthrough: 3 points to the answer at 3 down, Indian; Indian ink is a black drawing ink, and the whole is a Stoppard play title.
explanation.definitionFit: Indian is a kind of black drawing pigment, so ink is the class it belongs to.

clue.text: Criminal prepared to kidnap queen

indicators.note: the word for prepared seizes and holds the royal letter

parts.note: cooked means prepared, as food is
R, for Regina, is the abbreviation for queen

explanation.surface: A villain is all set to abduct the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Crooked as an adjective means dishonest or illegal, like a crook.

clue.text: God wants daughter to protect bird forever

definitions.note: an adverb here, but the answer is a noun: 'last forever' and 'last an eternity'

indicators.note: the trimmed word surrounds the bird
wants means lacks, so the letter for daughter goes

parts.note: a deity is a god
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A god asks a daughter to guard a bird for all time.
explanation.definitionFit: Eternity is endless time, so it is the state of lasting without end.

clue.text: Difficulty for retiring opera singer to sack alto

parts.note: pro means in favour of, for

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so the shortened name reads backwards
to sack is to dismiss, so the letter for alto is removed

parts.note: Nellie Melba, the Australian soprano

explanation.surface: Trouble for an ageing diva who must dismiss her alto.
explanation.walkthrough: Dame Nellie Melba was a famous Australian soprano, the opera singer here; the alto is dropped before the name is turned around.
explanation.definitionFit: A problem is a matter that causes trouble, a synonym for difficulty.

clue.text: One running out of clothes?

parts.note: reads as someone short of outfits, but describes a person running naked in public

explanation.walkthrough: 'Running out of' suggests having none left; it means literally running while out of one's clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A streaker dashes naked through a public place, typically a sports ground.

clue.text: Doctor close to pay agreement

parts.note: to doctor a patient is to treat them

indicators.note: only the last letter of pay is used

explanation.surface: A doctor nears a deal on pay.
explanation.definitionFit: A treaty is a formal pact between states, a type of accord.

clue.text: During two days US player once ran

indicators.note: the player sits within the two day letters

parts.note: D twice, D being the abbreviation for day
Arthur Ashe, the American tennis champion, who died in 1993

explanation.surface: An American sportsman once raced through a two-day event.
explanation.definitionFit: Dashed is a past tense of dash, meaning hurried or sprinted.

clue.text: Work out 2 ÷ 500

indicators.note: the division sign means the word for two is split by the numeral

parts.note: a deuce is a two in cards or dice
D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: An arithmetic exercise: calculate two divided by five hundred.
explanation.walkthrough: The sum looks like arithmetic, but the division sign means split: the word for two is divided by the Roman numeral for 500.
explanation.definitionFit: To deduce is to reason something to a conclusion, which is figuring it out.

clue.text: Provide excessively favourable conditions down under?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to pamper or cushion someone
second meaning: a bed stuffed with down, lying under you, read literally

explanation.walkthrough: 'Down under' wants to be Australia; it is the soft feathers beneath a sleeper.
explanation.definitionFit: To featherbed is to shield someone from hardship with generous treatment; a feather bed is a mattress filled with feathers.

clue.text: Multiple choice includes repetition

indicators.note: the phrase multiple choice holds the answer within its letters

explanation.surface: An exam format that keeps asking similar questions.
explanation.definitionFit: An echo is a sound repeated by reflection, so it is a reiteration.

clue.text: Fellow leaves capital £1,000 pine

indicators.note: the fellow leaves the city name, so those letters go

parts.note: London is the UK capital
a don is a university fellow
G for grand, slang for a thousand pounds

explanation.surface: An academic quits the capital with a thousand pounds and misses it.
explanation.definitionFit: To pine for something is to yearn, the verb sense of long.

clue.text: Desire to solve cryptic without thesaurus — finally!

indicators.note: cryptic means puzzling, so the letters of solve are jumbled
the letter named next is taken out before rearranging
only the last letter of thesaurus is used

explanation.definitionFit: Love is a strong affection or passion, close in sense to yearning.

clue.text: Choppers — helicopters transport emergency equipment to retiring leaders

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing, so the initials are read backwards
the first letters of each word lead it

explanation.surface: Choppers airlift emergency gear to leaders who are stepping down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Choppers' is set up as helicopters, but the answer is slang for teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: Choppers is informal slang for teeth, the things we bite with.

clue.text: Dig out old wine — terrible! It lacks body

parts.note: ex means former, old
cava is Spanish sparkling wine

indicators.note: only the ends of terrible remain, its middle gone

explanation.surface: Unearth an old wine and find it awful and thin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'body' sounds like wine tasting but means the middle of the word terrible.
explanation.definitionFit: To excavate is to unearth by removing soil, so it means unearth.
